name: Circus Lupus
label: Dischord
lede: Chris Thomson left Ignition's bass behind, took a microphone to Madison and then to Washington, and Dischord put out two albums of the result. Joan Jett produced a single on the way out.

eras.title: Madison, Wisconsin, and a singer who used to play bass
eras.text: Chris Thomson had played bass in DC's Ignition. At school in Madison he put the bass down, picked up the mic, and built a band around his words and a lot of jagged guitar.

years.h: Chris Thomson, late of Ignition, starts a band in Madison
years.p: [[Chris Thomson|e79601f0-2aa6-415c-886e-570aea8acea1]] sings, [[Chris Hamley|b3264bfd-2c4a-44fa-85f9-d2f9f293064d]] plays guitar, [[Arika Casebolt|4ffc2835-8d6d-4c82-adc6-19297bdedaf5]] drums and Reg Shrader plays bass. Dischord dates the band from spring 1990.

years.h: A nine-song cassette, later Dischord's LG1
years.p: Circus Lupus' 9 Song Demo is its first tape. Dischord carries it in its distribution catalog as LG1.

yt: Tightrope Walker / Chinese Nitro, both sides (audio)
years.h: Pittsburgh's Cubist Records puts out Tightrope Walker
years.p: The 7" pairs Tightrope Walker with Chinese Nitro. It's Circus Lupus' first single.

eras.title: Washington, and a label to go with it
eras.text: The move cost Circus Lupus its bassist and got it Dischord. In a town still measuring every band against Fugazi, Circus Lupus sounded more like the Fall: sideways vocals, riffs that seemed to fight each other.

years.cap: Circus Lupus on stage in Poznan, Poland, March 1993
years.h: Seth Lorinczi takes the bass as the band moves to D.C.
years.p: Reg Shrader doesn't make the move from Madison. [[Seth Lorinczi|ae764a61-4f4c-4018-b598-e14a8802a7f3]] takes his place and stays until Circus Lupus ends in 1993.
years.xp: Dischord says the band moved to Washington after its first 7" on Cubist, which is when Lorinczi joined. Trouser Press dates the move to 1991; Dischord gives no year.

years.h: Trenchmouth and Circus Lupus share a 7"
years.p: Chicago's Trenchmouth takes one side and Circus Lupus takes the other, with Sea of Serenity and Heathen. It's out on Skene! and Dischord, per Wikipedia.

q: Playing against one another in a race to get to the finish line.
yt: Live in Washington DC, July 3, 1992 (audience tape)
years.p: Circus Lupus' first album. Trouser Press heard Thomson in full Mark E. Smith mode, and a band proving punk still had teeth beyond [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]].
years.xp:
Trouser Press called it "a blast of energy in a cynical time" and said the players seemed to be in a race to the finish line, each against the others. Other reviewers reached for pinball: wailing vocals, snaking riffs, and what Team Rock called a scuzzy, grungy undercurrent.

The band toured it. Fans taped the shows, and three of those tapes are online: the JC Dobbs in Philadelphia on March 28, 1992, 924 Gilman in Berkeley on April 25, and a full set in Washington on July 3.

eras.title: Joan Jett in the booth, then the end
eras.text: Circus Lupus' last year brought Joan Jett to a Dischord single and a second album, Solid Brass, that pushed the angles further. By summer 1993 the band was done.

years.cap: Chris Thomson singing with Circus Lupus in Poznan, Poland, March 1993
years.p: Dischord's No. 73 pairs Pop Man with Pressure Point. The label says it was one of Jett's first production jobs since she worked with [[The Germs|42c4b58d-2e28-41d4-bfe5-4edee68386cf]] in 1979.
years.xp: Jett had produced the Germs' (GI) in 1979, which is the line Dischord draws between that job and this one. Both songs later rode along at the end of Solid Brass, next to a second, different version of Pop Man.

years.h: Solid Brass is Dischord No. 79 and the last album
years.p: Trouser Press on Circus Lupus' second album, recorded at Inner Ear.
years.xp: Song titles include Right Turn Clyde, New Cop Car and Deviant Gesture Catalog.

years.cap: Circus Lupus at the 007 Club, Prague, March 1993
years.h: Summer 1993, and Circus Lupus is over
years.p: Dischord gives the run as spring 1990 to summer 1993: three years, two albums, a handful of singles.

eras.title: Three bands from one
eras.text: The band split down the middle. Hamley, Lorinczi and Casebolt carried on as Antimony, Thomson went his own way, and later he and Hamley reunited in The Monorchid.

years.p: Chris Hamley, Seth Lorinczi and Arika Casebolt release Phantom Itch, which Trouser Press said carried on Circus Lupus' thorny dynamism. Thomson starts the groove-punk band [[Las Mordidas|6e471c60-ce00-4d4e-a2af-b61fa6e95574]].
Trouser Press lists Andy Cone, Andy Coronado and Tom Allnutt alongside them. Let Them Eat Monorchid comes in 1996, and Who Put Out the Fire? in 1998, after the band ended.
years.xp: Seth Lorinczi later formed [[The Quails|1c87cd77-3048-4e06-96e6-f5a52b5f60e9]] in San Francisco.

years.p: Dischord reissues the first album, per Wikipedia. Solid Brass is out of print on CD and LP and lives on digitally.
